advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Broaden the provisioning exception handling in the collection hook (and fixture fallbacks) so unexpected OS/lock errors record a skip reason rather than aborting collection for the whole e2e tier.
evidence: conftest.py:79-82: `try: provision_toolchain(...) except ToolchainProvisioningError as exc: _PROVISION_ERROR = str(exc)`
_toolchain.py:73: `js_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` and 74-75 open/flock — these can raise OSError, which is NOT a ToolchainProvisioningError.
The fixture fallbacks (conftest.py:99-102, 141-144) have the same narrow except, so a non-ToolchainProvisioningError there aborts the test instead of skipping.
advisory.finding: `pytest_collection_modifyitems` only catches `ToolchainProvisioningError`. Any other exception raised during provisioning (e.g. an OSError from `js_dir.mkdir` in `_install_lock`, a permission error on the lock file, or a fcntl error) propagates out of the collection hook and aborts collection for the entire e2e tier, rather than degrading to a skip as the tier's opt-in/self-skipping contract promises.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin actions/setup-node to an exact Node version (e.g. '22.x.y' or a committed .node-version/.nvmrc) rather than the floating major '22'.
evidence: `node-version: '22'`
Commit message claims: "with the Node version itself pinned rather than inherited from the runner image"

A bare major ('22') resolves to whatever latest 22.x setup-node's manifest offers at run time; the cache key uses `steps.e2e-node.outputs.node-version` which mitigates cache poisoning but not the drift itself.
advisory.finding: The e2e Node toolchain is pinned only to major version '22' in actions/setup-node, so minor/patch Node upgrades can still silently change the toolchain despite the stated goal of pinning; reproducibility is only partially guaranteed.
scenarios: A new Node 22.x patch lands and changes esbuild bundle output or npm behavior between otherwise-identical CI runs.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use an exact node-version (e.g. via a committed `.nvmrc`/`node-version-file`) so the toolchain is fully reproducible.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile `make e2e-deps` with the optional-dependency split (decide whether the portable path should install the browser stack) and document the intended footprint.
evidence: `cd tests/e2e/js && npm ci && npm run build`
package.json now declares `"optionalDependencies": { "playwright": "^1.61.0" }`
conftest passes `with_browser=` and `_toolchain.py` uses `OMIT_BROWSER_FLAG = "--omit=optional"` for non-browser runs, but the Makefile does not.
advisory.finding: The `make e2e-deps` target runs `npm ci` without `--omit=optional`, so the portable/CI path installs the full tree including the now-optional playwright browser stack, diverging from the conftest provisioning which omits it for non-browser selections; the manifest split into optionalDependencies is not honored uniformly across provisioning paths.
scenarios: CI runs `make e2e-deps` and installs playwright (~16.8M) even when no browser test is selected, undercutting the stated bill-reduction rationale.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that runs `make e2e-deps` with a stub PATH containing npm but not node and asserts it exits 0 with the skip message (and does not invoke `npm ci`).
evidence: Makefile:468-473: `@# Both binaries are required: ... an npm-but-no-node host would install successfully and then fail every e2e test.` followed by `@if ! command -v npm ... || ! command -v node ...; then echo ...; exit 0; fi;`

test_the_portable_make_target_provisions_with_npm_ci runs `make -n e2e-deps` (dry-run) and only asserts `'npm ci' in recipe` / `'run build' in recipe` — the printed recipe text is identical whether or not the runtime guard would fire, so the guard's behavior is unverified
provision_toolchain only checks `shutil.which('npm')` (_toolchain.py:133-137); the node-presence requirement exists solely in this Makefile branch, so no other test covers it
Named violating input: a host with `npm` on PATH but `node` absent — the guard's exit-0-skip on this input is asserted nowhere
advisory.finding: The newly added Makefile `e2e-deps` guard requiring BOTH `npm` and `node` on PATH (skipping with `exit 0` when either is missing) is untested. `test_the_portable_make_target_provisions_with_npm_ci` only inspects `make -n e2e-deps` dry-run output, which prints the recipe text without executing the `command -v` conditional, so the npm-present-but-node-absent skip path — the exact host the comment says the guard exists for — is never exercised.
scenarios: A host or CI lane with npm installed but node missing runs `make e2e-deps`; if the guard regressed to run `npm ci` unconditionally, no test would catch it
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that sets PATH to a bin dir with a stub `npm` but no `node`, runs `subprocess.run(['make','e2e-deps'], cwd=_REPO_ROOT, ...)`, and asserts returncode==0, that the skip message is emitted, and that npm was not invoked (e.g. no node_modules created / empty npm-calls.log).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the e2e Node version in a single source of truth (e.g. package.json `engines` / `.nvmrc`) that both CI setup-node and `make e2e-deps` honor, rather than pinning only in the workflow.
evidence: .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:464-465: `node-version: '22'`

.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:457-459 comment: "Pin the toolchain rather than inheriting whatever Node the runner image happens to ship: an image bump would otherwise silently change what the e2e tier builds and runs."
Makefile:470-474: `if ! command -v npm ... || ! command -v node ...; then ... fi; cd tests/e2e/js && npm ci && npm run build` — no version pin/check
ABSENCE: no `engines` field in tests/e2e/js/package.json diff and no `.nvmrc` added; the portable path never asserts a Node major
advisory.finding: The e2e Node toolchain version is pinned to Node 22 only in the CI workflow (`actions/setup-node` with `node-version: '22'`), but the portable `make e2e-deps` target and the in-fixture fallback in `_toolchain.py` invoke whatever `node`/`npm` happen to be on PATH. There is no shared version-of-record (e.g. `.nvmrc`, `package.json` `engines`, or a version file) enforced by the make target, so a developer's local build and the CI build can provision and bundle against different Node majors — reintroducing exactly the 'silently changes what the e2e tier builds and runs' drift the CI comment says pinning avoids.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the npm cache prefix restore-key cannot serve a stale/partial `~/.npm` store when the lockfile changes, or drop the prefix fallback.
evidence: .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:474-476: `key: ${{ runner.os }}-npm-${{ steps.e2e-node.outputs.node-version }}-${{ hashFiles('tests/e2e/js/package-lock.json') }}` / `restore-keys: ${{ runner.os }}-npm-${{ steps.e2e-node.outputs.node-version }}-`
package-lock.json diff moves playwright from devDependencies to optionalDependencies and CI installs with `--omit=optional` conditionally
advisory.finding: The npm cache `restore-keys` prefix (`${{ runner.os }}-npm-${{ steps.e2e-node.outputs.node-version }}-`) drops the lockfile hash, so a cache populated under an earlier `package-lock.json` can be restored for a build with a changed lockfile. Because the change also converts `playwright` to an optionalDependency and CI provisions with `--omit=optional` when no browser test is selected, a restored `~/.npm` from a browser-including run (or vice versa) can carry a package set that no longer matches the current selection. With `npm ci` this is a download-avoidance store rather than the installed tree, so drift is bounded, but the prefix-only restore-key is worth confirming it cannot serve a partially-populated store.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and document whether a failed `npm ci`/`npm run build` in `make e2e-deps` should hard-fail CI or self-skip; if self-skip is intended (matching the in-fixture fallback), tolerate the failure rather than propagating a non-zero exit.
evidence: Makefile:474: `cd tests/e2e/js && npm ci && npm run build`
conftest.py:13-15: 'When Node is absent or provisioning fails (offline CI, etc.) the whole tier skips with a clear reason rather than failing — the Python unit tests remain the always-on floor.'

The Makefile only guards against absent node/npm (lines 470-473, `exit 0`); once both are present a network/registry error from `npm ci` propagates as a non-zero make exit and fails the CI step, where previously the fixture called `pytest.skip(f"e2e: `npm install` failed (offline?)...")`.
blocking.finding: `make e2e-deps` runs `npm ci && npm run build` with no failure tolerance, so a transient npm/registry failure or offline runner hard-fails the CI 'Install rebar' step. This contradicts the documented design that the e2e tier is self-skipping and that provisioning failure (offline CI, etc.) should skip rather than fail — a contract the removed in-fixture path honored via pytest.skip.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the CI e2e-deps probe distinguish a genuinely-absent rule from other `make -n` failures (e.g. grep the target list, or fail loudly on unexpected make errors) so a broken Makefile does not silently re-enable in-fixture provisioning.
evidence: `if [ '${{ matrix.os }}' != 'macos-latest' ] && make -n e2e-deps >/dev/null 2>&1; then`
`echo "::notice::skipping e2e toolchain provisioning (no e2e-deps rule on this tree, or macOS lane)"`

The comment frames this purely as a 'PREDATES-THE-GATE guard' for a missing rule, but `make -n` returns non-zero for other reasons too (missing binary, Makefile syntax error), all of which take the silent-skip branch — the probe cannot distinguish 'rule absent' from 'probe itself failed'.
dropped.finding: The CI provisioning gate `make -n e2e-deps >/dev/null 2>&1` fails OPEN: it silently skips provisioning for ANY make failure, not only a missing `e2e-deps` rule. A Makefile parse error in the patchset, `make` absent, or any other non-zero `make -n` exit is indistinguishable from 'rule not present' — CI emits a `::notice::` and skips, so the e2e tests fall back to in-fixture provisioning charged to the 300s pytest-timeout budget, reintroducing exactly bug 9a17-e0b3-7aa6-4091.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the bundle is only observable as complete: write dist/roundtrip.mjs to a temp path and atomically rename, or make _satisfied()'s bundle check meaningful only after acquiring the flock (or write a completion sentinel under the lock).
evidence: Shared resource: `dist/roundtrip.mjs` — `bundle = js_dir / BUNDLE_RELPATH` (_toolchain.py:129), written by `_run_step("npm run build", ...)` inside the lock (_toolchain.py:152-153)

Two executors: xdist worker processes under `-n 4 --dist worksteal`, each running the session fixture (conftest.py comment lines 63-64: 'under -n 4 --dist worksteal every worker runs the fixture'); concurrency also exercised by test_two_concurrent_workers_do_not_overlap_their_install_steps
READ (outside lock): `if _satisfied(js_dir, with_browser=with_browser): return` (_toolchain.py:130) where `_satisfied` returns on `(js_dir / BUNDLE_RELPATH).is_file()` (_toolchain.py:103)

WRITE (inside lock): esbuild `roundtrip.mjs --bundle ... --outfile=dist/roundtrip.mjs` (package.json:8) run via `_run_step("npm run build", [npm, "run", "build"], js_dir, build_timeout)` (_toolchain.py:153) inside `with _install_lock(js_dir):` (_toolchain.py:143)

Guard the writer uses but this reader omits: `fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)` (_toolchain.py:75). The line-130 read is not under that lock; the re-check at line 147 IS, but a reader whose line-130 check already saw the file exist returns before ever reaching line 143.

Harm: a worker reads a truncated/partial `dist/roundtrip.mjs`, treats provisioning as complete, then `node dist/roundtrip.mjs` (conftest.py:107) fails to parse the incomplete bundle — a spurious e2e failure rather than a clean skip/pass.
dropped.finding: The pre-lock `_satisfied()` short-circuit reads the shared bundle file `dist/roundtrip.mjs` (existence check) OUTSIDE the flock that its writer holds, so a worker can observe a partially-written bundle produced by a peer's concurrent esbuild build and skip provisioning as 'done'.
scenarios: First cold provisioning: worker A holds the lock and is mid-esbuild-write of dist/roundtrip.mjs; worker B's _satisfied() at line 130 sees the file already created (esbuild --outfile is not a guaranteed atomic create-temp-then-rename) and returns, then runs a test that executes the half-written bundle.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the `with_browser`/`--omit=optional` install-size optimization in provision_toolchain() belongs to ticket 9a17 or split it into its own ticket.
evidence: tests/e2e/_toolchain.py:52 `BROWSER_PACKAGE = "playwright"`
tests/e2e/_toolchain.py:53 `OMIT_BROWSER_FLAG = "--omit=optional"`
tests/e2e/_toolchain.py:120 `That is the cheap half of the fix: a selection with no browser test installs 11 packages instead of 15 and 12M instead of 30M.`
Union scope names only `provision_toolchain()` with explicit per-step `timeout=`, a step-naming `ToolchainProvisioningError`, and the cross-process lock — no browser/install-size optimization
dropped.finding: The provision_toolchain() browser-stack omission optimization (with_browser param, --omit=optional, playwright-aware _satisfied() re-check) is an install-size performance refactor not authorized by ticket 9a17, whose scope/AC covers only per-step timeouts, a step-naming error, the cross-process lock, the make target, and the CI cache.
dropped.suggested_fix: Split the browser-stack omission optimization (with_browser, OMIT_BROWSER_FLAG, playwright-aware _satisfied) into its own performance ticket; keep 9a17 to the timeout/named-error/lock/make/cache scope.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the browser_runner provisioning integration is authorized by ticket 9a17 (which names only bpmn_harness) or move it to the browser-stack ticket.
evidence: tests/e2e/conftest.py:42 `_TOOLCHAIN_FIXTURES = frozenset({"bpmn_harness", _BROWSER_FIXTURE})`
tests/e2e/conftest.py:80 `provision_toolchain(_JS_DIR, with_browser=_BROWSER_FIXTURE in selected)`
tests/e2e/conftest.py:139-144 browser_runner re-reports _PROVISION_ERROR and calls provision_toolchain(with_browser=True)
